transcript.content: Hi, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

I keep forgetting everyday things—appointments, errands, even important family plans—and it’s starting to cause problems at home. It has gotten much more noticeable and disruptive over the last year and a half, especially since I scaled back my consulting work and lost the rigid schedule I used to rely on to keep myself on track.

Before the past year and a half, did you have similar problems with attention, forgetfulness, or staying organized going back to childhood or your school years? Or is this a newer change that started only recently?

These issues actually go all the way back to my childhood, even though they've only recently become this disruptive. When I was in elementary school, my teachers often noted that I was bright but constantly daydreaming, chatting, and forgetting to turn in completed homework. My parents also used to joke that I was always "off in my own world" instead of finishing my chores.
Do these attention and organization problems happen in more than one part of your life, like at home, work, and in social situations? Can you give one or two examples from different settings?

Yes, they definitely affect multiple areas, specifically at home and in my community volunteer work. At home, I've missed important things like my son's parent-teacher meetings and soccer pickups, which causes a lot of tension with my husband. During our neighborhood garden planning, I'll often make careless mistakes on our quarterly budget or interrupt others by blurting out ideas before they finish speaking.
Before age 12, did these attention or impulsive behaviors clearly cause problems at school, at home, or with friends? What kinds of problems did they lead to back then?

Back then, it mostly caused constant friction at school and home rather than major failures, like getting scolded for not finishing my chores because I was daydreaming. At school, I'd lose points on my grades simply because I forgot to hand in homework I'd actually completed, and I was often reprimanded for chatting too much during class.

During the past year and a half, have you also had depression, anxiety, major stress, sleep problems, or memory changes that seemed new or out of proportion to your lifelong attention issues? Or does this feel mainly like the same attention and organization problems you’ve always had, just more obvious without a strict schedule?

It definitely feels like the same lifelong attention struggles I've always had, rather than a new issue like depression or anxiety. These problems just became much more obvious over the last 18 months because I lost the rigid consulting schedule that previously kept my childhood tendencies hidden.
